title: The Last Ember Anew
premise: Freya Ishikawa, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead through her carvings, discovers their own name and today's date in a century-old prophecy book smuggled through the Thornfell mountains. The prophecy names them as the Emberbearer — the one who must return a stolen shard of the old gods' fire to its resting place before the solstice, or reignite the war that once shattered the mountain clans. Hunted by the Ashen Order, who want the shard to finish what their ancestors started, Freya gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced Order defector, a ghost who remembers dying for the ember, and a rival smuggler with debts of his own. At the solstice, Freya chooses not to restore or destroy the ember but to give it to the dead themselves, dissolving the prophecy — and finding, at last, that belonging is something you build, not inherit.
about_author: Theo Vasquez is a former trail guide who spent five years leading expeditions through remote mountain passes before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy rooted in landscapes they've walked, exploring how strangers become family in the wild places between destinations.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. While carving a commission from smuggled bone, Freya hears a dead woman's voice warning of fire, then finds their own name and tonight's date inked in a prophecy book hidden in a client's cargo. The emotional beat is vertigo — the solid, known world of roads and routes suddenly unreadable.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following the dead woman's voice to a collapsed shrine, Freya unearths the ember shard, which burns cold and speaks in a chorus of every voice they've ever carved. The Order's hunters arrive; Freya flees into the high passes, carrying the thing everyone wants. Beat: reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: A Defector's Debt
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian Vane, an Ashen Order knight who abandoned his post after seeing what the Order did to a village, intercepts Freya intending to take the shard — and instead saves them from his former brothers. Beat: shame curdling into the first fragile choice toward redemption.

chapters.title: The Ghost Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Maren-the-ghost's POV (rendered as memory-fragments). Maren, the dead woman whose bones Freya carved, reveals she was the last Emberbearer, killed a century ago by the Order — and that she chose Freya deliberately. Beat: grief transmuted into trust; Freya realizes they were chosen, not cursed.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Honor
chapters.summary: Rurik's POV. Rurik Ostrov, a rival smuggler who owes Freya a blood-debt, offers safe passage through the lowlands in exchange for a cut of whatever the shard sells for. His mercenary cynicism masks loneliness. Beat: transactional alliance beginning to feel like companionship around a shared campfire.

chapters.title: The Order Closes In
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Order burns the mountain waystations, cutting off escape, and Cassian's former mentor offers him amnesty if he betrays the group. He refuses aloud — but Freya overhears the offer and doubts him. Beat: the found family's first fracture, trust tested by old wounds.

chapters.title: Prophecy's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In the drowned archive beneath Lake Verren, Maren shows Freya the prophecy's erased second half: the Emberbearer was always meant to die delivering the ember. The war doesn't end with victory — it ends with sacrifice. Beat: despair; Freya rages at being a tool of dead people's plans.

chapters.title: Ashfall
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. The Order ambushes them at the pass; Rurik takes a mortal wound buying time, and dies asking Freya to carve his name so he won't be forgotten. Cassian holds the line against his mentor. Beat: devastating cost — the family pays in blood, and Freya learns what the shard truly is: the accumulated dead, yearning to be heard.

chapters.title: The Solstice Choice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the ember's resting place, Freya refuses both fates — restoration or death. Instead they carve every name the shard carries into the mountain itself, releasing the dead from the ember and the prophecy from its authors. The Order's power collapses as their founding lie burns away. Beat: defiant transcendence; rewriting inheritance instead of fulfilling it.

chapters.title: Carved Names, Living Hands
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue-like. A season later, Freya's workshop has become a refuge for strays and deserters; Cassian stays without being asked, and Maren's voice rests quiet at last. Freya carves Rurik's name beside the others. Beat: warm resolution — belonging built by hand, one name at a time.
